title: Shelf Walls and the Quick-Swap Trick
lead: Shelves show off your best stuff, 3 items on each one. Give them power, and one tap swaps your whole hotbar.

steps.title: Build a frame
steps.text: Put a row of Dark Oak Planks along a wall. Leave a gap 2 blocks high above it. Then add a ledge of upside-down Dark Oak Stairs on top.

steps.title: Hang the shelves
steps.text: Place 6 Birch Shelves in the gap, in 2 rows of 3. The dark frame around them makes the pale shelves stand out.

steps.title: Fill them up
steps.text: Hold an item and use a shelf slot. The item goes on the shelf. Each shelf holds 3 items, so this wall shows 18.

steps.title: Power the bottom row
steps.text: Swap the 3 blocks under the bottom row for Blocks of Redstone. Now those shelves have power, and their fronts change. Three powered shelves side by side join up.

steps.title: Swap!
steps.text: Use any shelf in the powered row. All 9 items swap with your 9 hotbar slots at once. Use it again to swap back.

body: A shelf holds 3 stacks of items and shows them on the front. Use shelves for trophy walls, shops, kitchens and libraries.
With no power, each slot works on its own. Using a slot swaps the item in your hand with the item on the shelf.
With power, the shelf swaps with your hotbar instead. One shelf swaps 3 slots. Two joined shelves swap 6. Three swap all 9.
Want a switch to turn the swap on and off? Build the Shelf Quick-Swap Armory in the Redstone Workshop.
tips: Put 6 stripped logs of one wood in a crafting table. Fill the top row and the bottom row. You get 6 shelves.
In Bedrock, powered shelves join up even when they are made of different woods. Just make them face the same way.
A shelf shows the item but not how many there are. A full stack looks just like one.
In Bedrock, you cannot put a torch, button or lever on a shelf. Power it from the block underneath instead.
challenge: Make a powered row of 3 shelves by your front door. Fill it with a building kit, and swap it in whenever you start a build.
